subject: Re: Hosted API — tiered response window & exception request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@helixai.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixai.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API — latency commitments and measurement windows

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team appreciated the walkthrough of batching and KV cache optimizations. We are moving fast on the procurement side, but one outstanding item from our SRE team is the exact language around latency SLOs for the hosted API.

Specifically, Helix needs firm commitments for p50 and p95 across customer-facing inference (interactive chat) under our expected load profile, plus a documented carveout strategy for short bursty spikes (we have a predictable weekly sync that can temporarily triple RPS for ~2–5 minutes).

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood commit to p50/p95 numbers measured over a preservation window (your typical 5m aggregation) or are you proposing a different aggregation cadence?
- If you need an exception for the weekly burst, what would the formal exception look like (time-bounded, regional carveout, or request-based)?

Procurement also asked whether an exception would affect the standard SLA credits and whether any fallback model variants are considered ‘compatible’ for the purposes of uptime calculation.

I attached a small sample of our traffic (anonymized) so you can see the burst pattern. Can you put together a short proposal we can route to our legal and SRE teams?

Best,
Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
Helix AI

--- attachment: helix-traffic-sample.csv (text/csv)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@helixai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — latency commitments and measurement windows

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and for the sample traffic. I ran the CSV through our measurement tooling and sketched a response we think will meet both Helix’s availability expectations and our operational constraints. High-level summary below; attached is a short PDF with the windows and example contract language.

Proposal (high level):
- Base commitments (global, hosted API): p50 <= 65ms, p95 <= 220ms, measured over 1-minute rolling quantiles and reported on hourly aggregates.
- Tiered measurement windows:
  - Normal: global 1-minute rolling quantiles, hourly reporting (applies 99% of minutes).
  - Bursts carveout: automated short-window carveout for transient spikes up to 10 consecutive minutes once per day per region if triggered by amplified legitimate traffic patterns (e.g., Helix weekly sync).
  - Transient network incidents: regional 30-minute carveouts which require post-incident RCA and mitigation plan to avoid repeated carveouts.
- Exception mechanics: Helix can request a scheduled carveout for a recurring sync (provide cron/UTC window). For unscheduled bursts, our detection will auto-apply a single short carveout (up to 10 minutes) if traffic parameters match the supplied pattern; additional events require review.
- SLA credits: Carveouts exclude minutes from SLA calculations; credits only apply to non-carveout minutes where Redwood misses p95 commitments. Carveout allowances are finite in the contract (e.g., 12 auto carveouts per 90 days) to prevent abuse.
- Fallback models: We propose automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-cost variant (quantized) for best-effort requests — fallbacks count as served for uptime so long as API contract-level response schema is preserved. We will document compatible model families in the contract appendix.

Next steps: Ben can help size reserved burst capacity if you want guaranteed headroom rather than carveouts. Marissa, can you confirm if there are any internal limits on how many carveouts we can promise in a single enterprise contract?

I attached the proposal PDF and included a one-page example clause you can send to legal. Happy to jump on a short call with your SREs to walk through detection thresholds.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

--- attachments: redwood-tiered-window-proposal.pdf (application/pdf)

From: procurement@helixai.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@helixai.com>, legal@helixai.com
Date: 2026-10-26T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — latency commitments and measurement windows

Olga / Ben — reviewed the PDF with our SRE and legal. A few clarifying points before we escalate to signatures:
1) The proposed p95 = 220ms baseline is acceptable, but we need the measurement definition explicitly called out: does 1-minute rolling quantile mean you compute the p95 across requests in that minute, then exclude minutes within carveouts before you compute hourly aggregates? Please add a worked example (minute counts, how you treat empty minutes).
2) For the recurring scheduled carveout, we need the ability to define it as a fixed UTC window (e.g., Tuesdays 03:00–03:10 UTC) and guarantee that auto-carveouts do not consume the daily auto carveout slot if pre-scheduled.
3) Credits formula: request the exact SLA credit schedule for missing p95 (e.g., % of monthly fee per hour of missed minutes).
4) Fallback models: confirmed that fallback responses count toward uptime is fine only if they are pin-compatible in schema and privacy matches (no truncation of user-provided context). Please confirm that fallbacks will not access customer context beyond what the primary model has access to.

Can you provide a redlined clause and an example credit schedule? Once we have those, we can route to signatures.

Procurement
Helix AI

--- note: please include example credit table in next doc

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: procurement@helixai.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@helixai.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — latency commitments and measurement windows

Hi Jordan / Procurement — quick answers inline and attached a one-page credit schedule and a sample worked example of measurement calculations.

Quick notes:
- Measurement worked example: we compute p95 per 1-minute bucket (only minutes with >=5 requests are considered valid for quantile calculation; minutes with <5 requests are excluded from the hourly aggregate). Carveout minutes are removed entirely before hourly aggregation. Example attached shows a 60-minute hour with 57 valid minutes, 2 carved minutes, 1 low-volume minute — effective hourly p95 computed across the 57 valid minutes.
- Scheduled carveouts: you can register a recurring UTC window. Registered scheduled windows do not decrement the daily auto-carveout allotment. Unscheduled auto-carveouts are limited to 12 per 90 days as proposed.
- Credits: attached schedule: 5% of monthly hosted fee for each 60-minute window where effective hourly p95 > committed p95, capped at 50%/month. Credits only apply to non-carveout minutes.
- Fallback models and data access: fallbacks operate within the same tenancy and do not access extra customer context. If a fallback changes tokenization/formatting we will surface that in the appendix; fallbacks will be listed per model family.

Attachments: redwood-tiered-window-proposal.pdf (updated), redwood-sla-credit-schedule-v1.pdf, measurement-worked-example.txt

If this looks good we can provide contract language and a clean appendix for model compatibility next week. Happy to do a 30-minute call to finalize.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
